interest: This file is valuable to historians of interwar Japan and U.S.-Japan relations as it illustrates the State Department's monitoring of Japan's economic crisis during the onset of the Great Depression in 1930. The entries highlight both public-sector relief initiatives—specifically Japanese government plans to extend loans to struggling small merchants and industrialists—and private-sector financial coordination, notably meetings among Tokyo syndicate bank leaders to establish a joint credit investigation organ for industrial rationalization. Furthermore, the document offers insight into State Department archival and record-keeping procedures, showing how substantive economic despatches from diplomats William R. Castle, Jr. and Edwin L. Neville were classified under periodic political reports (894.00 P.R.) and cross-referenced on Form DS-46 under the specific decimal file for rural credits and cooperative systems (894.5032).
overview: This file (decimal file 894.5032, File 257) consists of a Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) titled 'Cooperative Systems -- Rural Credits in Japan.' The sheet indexes two cross-referenced communications from 1930 regarding financial relief and banking rationalization in Japan during the onset of the Great Depression. The first entry, dated April 7, 1930, cross-references Despatch No. 91 from Ambassador William R. Castle, Jr. (filed under 894.00 P.R./28, enclosing Report No. 42), which reported on Japanese government plans to assist small merchants and industrialists hard hit by economic distress. The second entry, dated August 1, 1930, cross-references Despatch No. 219 from Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville (filed under 894.00 P.R./32), detailing meetings of syndicate bank leaders in Tokyo to establish a joint credit investigation organ to facilitate organized credit accommodation for industrial rationalization.
